newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude craters at session's end on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude craters at session's end on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices cratered Tuesday when technical sell stops were triggered after unease about Iraqi crude sales and weather forecasts sent prices lower, said traders.
"You can definitely attribute some of this to heating oil and the weather, but so much of it was technical when stops went off below $25.00," said a New York trader.

January crude ended off 88 cents at $24.42 a barrel after falling as much as $1.02 to $24.28. January heating oil ended down 2.51 cents at 69.62 cents a gallon while Jan gasoline ended off 2.02 cents at 66.86 cents a gallon in sympathy.
The National Weather Service's six to 10 day outlook released Monday called for above normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
On Tuesday, Iraq submitted two oil contracts to the United Nations for the sale of its crude under the U.N. oil-for-deal.

"There is a lot indication that if they (Iraq) can move oil, then they will. That created selling pressure in a continuation from yesterday," said Merrill Lynch senior energy futures analyst Michael Rothman.
Chartists pegged support for prompt crude at $24.00 and, after that, at around $23.50.
Under the deal, the United Nations will ease sanctions against Iraq and will allow Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, in exchange for humanitarian aid.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in a statement Tuesday that Iraq hoped to double the amount of oil it is allowed to ship to world markets after three months.

One chartist in Washington D.C. said Tuesday's crude action was evidence that the January contract high of $25.70 last Friday was the top of a failed fifth advancing wave in an Elliott Wave pattern. Crude's post-Gulf War high of $26.10 on October 22 was the top of the third wave, the chartist said.

"It's our view that the market has completed a five wave advance, and we are now entering an extended correction," the chartist said. He added the first corrective wave could extend to $22.10, closing the price gap made on September 3 that extends to $22.38 on a spot continuation chart.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
